parakeet: Religious dependency makes freedom feel like fear. Ever wonder why so many people stay in toxic, restrictive belief systems? Even when they know deep down something isn't right? Because religion doesn't just shape how you think, it shapes what you fear. It convinces you that life without faith is terrifying, empty, and meaningless. Without God, you will have no purpose. Without faith, you will be lost and alone. Without belief, life is cold, dark, and hopeless. But here's the reality. Those aren't facts, those are threats. And threats are how religions keep people dependent. If faith were truly empowering, people wouldn't be scared to leave it. If religion truly gave people joy, peace, and strength, then walking away wouldn't feel like losing a part of yourself. But that's exactly the point. Faith is designed to bind itself to your identity so that questioning it feels like questioning your own existence. That's why religious people say things like, I don't know who I'd be without the Lord. If I stop believing, my whole world would collapse. Without God, life wouldn't be worth living. That's not belief, that's psychological dependency. It's the same dynamic as an abusive relationship, where someone says, You'll never find anyone else who loves you like I do. If you leave, you will be alone and miserable. You need me more than I need you. The goal isn't to actually empower you, it's to make sure you never walk away. Think of a child raised their whole life to believe that monsters lived outside their house. They're told if you leave, you'll be in danger. They're warned you won't survive without us. They're convinced the world outside is dark, hopeless, and cruel. That child will likely grow up terrified to leave, even if there's real terror within the house itself. That's what religion does to people. It trains them to fear the unknown so they never question their captivity. Fear-based dependency is not faith and it's not love, it's control. And control only works as long as you stay afraid. But what happens when you stop fearing the unknown? What happens when you stop believing in threats? You take your first real step towards freedom. Because the truth is, life without faith is not meaningless, it's yours. No guilt, no fear, no limits. Just you in full control of your own story. And that that's what religion never wanted you to discover.
